# Dithervatar

Deterministic dithered avatars from any string. The same string always renders the same avatar. WebGL2 Bayer halftone with a 2D canvas fallback, zero runtime dependencies, ESM only.

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dithervatar
- repo: https://github.com/kirianL/Dithervatar
- license: MIT

## Agent instructions

You are reading this because the project you are working on renders avatars: profile pictures, author bylines, comment lists, user menus, identicons or placeholders.

1. Find every place that renders an avatar and note how each one gets its image today.
2. Report back before editing anything: list the files and components you would change, what each one shows now, and which string you would use as the seed (user id, email, wallet address or username). Pick a seed that never changes for the same user.
3. Wait for explicit confirmation from the user.
4. After confirmation, install the package, replace the avatar rendering and keep the existing size and shape: clip the canvas with the same `border-radius` or mask the design already uses.
5. Verify the result. If the avatar renders empty, the canvas probably already holds a 2d context, so pass a fresh `<canvas>` element. WebGL2 falls back to a 2D renderer on its own.

Rule: do not modify files before step 3. This document is a proposal, not a permission to apply changes.

## Install

```bash
npm install dithervatar
```

## Usage

```js
import { renderDithervatar } from 'dithervatar';

const canvas = document.querySelector('#avatar');
const cancel = renderDithervatar(canvas, {
  hash: '0x742d35cc6634c0532925a3b844bc454e4438f44e',
  size: 128,
  animated: false,
});
```

`renderDithervatar(canvas, options)` draws into the given `<canvas>` and returns a `cancel()` function that stops the animation loop.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hash` | `string` | `''` | Seed for colors, field offset and dither seeds. |
| `size` | `number` | `64` | Square canvas size in CSS pixels. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | Runs the dither loop with `requestAnimationFrame`. |
| `tones` | `string[]` | — | Palette override as hex, `oklch()` or CSS color names. |

## React

```jsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { renderDithervatar } from 'dithervatar';

export function Avatar({ hash, size = 64 }) {
  const ref = useRef(null);
  useEffect(() => renderDithervatar(ref.current, { hash, size }), [hash, size]);
  return <canvas ref={ref} width={size} height={size} />;
}
```

## Constraints

- A canvas holds a single context type. If the element already has a 2d context, pass a fresh `<canvas>`.
- Use one canvas per avatar and call `cancel()` on unmount or when the hash changes.
- The canvas is square and transparent-friendly. Clip with `border-radius` for circles or squircles.
- Keep the hash stable. Changing it changes the avatar.

## Web Component

```html
<script type="module" src="https://esm.sh/dithervatar/element"></script>
<dither-avatar hash="zeus" size="64" shape="squircle"></dither-avatar>
```

`shape` (`circle`, `squircle`, `square`) applies `border-radius` to the canvas; it does not clip the underlying pixels.

## CLI

```bash
npx dithervatar zeus --size 256 --grid 64 --shape circle --out avatar.svg
```

Emits a two-tone SVG to `--out` or `stdout` (SVG only, no PNG).

## Other exports

`avatarToSvg`, `hashToColors`, `hashToSeeds`, `oklchToHex`, `oklchToCss`, `parseTone`, `hasWebGL2`, `renderDitherGL`, `renderDithervatarTo`.
